Use case: background-extraction and precise-object-edit. Edit the provided game restoration atlas into a TRUE TRANSPARENT RGBA sprite atlas. This is a production alignment asset, not a new scene. Keep exactly TWO equal columns by THREE equal rows, same panel order. Extract ONLY the named foreground landmark and its immediate structural footings from panels 1–5. Remove all sky, distant landscape, water, broad terrain, shadows cast on the wider ground, characters, scenery and all text. Panel 6 must be completely transparent. Do not paint a checkerboard. Preserve the painterly detail, original landmark design, material colors and five progress states: ruined, initial repair, nearly complete, restored, celebrated. Crucially REGISTER all five versions: identical camera/perspective, identical ground-contact baseline and identical structural foundation width and centre within each cell. Each cell is a fixed landscape 3:2 canvas. Put the common foundation endpoints at x=12% and x=88%, base contact at y=88% of its cell; tallest completed landmark fits above y=10%. Construction scaffolding and decorations can extend beyond the foundation but must remain inside the cell. Do not scale each stage to fill the cell independently. The same physical stones/posts must occupy the same pixel positions whenever they remain between stages. Ruined stages must be solid painted objects, not translucent. Generous transparent padding around all objects, no touching neighboring cells. Output square atlas if possible, with genuine alpha, not a solid black or white background.
Landmark to extract: Zero Marsh’s mossy stone arch, narrow stone causeway and three bronze lantern posts. Keep the same arch and paving in all stages; neglected overgrown paving first, cleared first bank/post second, all posts and clean path third, golden lanterns lit fourth, ribbons fifth. Remove all fog, trees, water, reeds and wide terrain. The mist will be a separate layer in the game.
